newsitem.title: USA: Pact between NYC and NYS comptroller breaks down.
newsitem.headline: Pact between NYC and NYS comptroller breaks down.

text.p: New York City's pact with the state comptroller over his audits of several city departments fell apart late Monday evening, said a spokeswoman for the state comptroller, H. Carl McCall.

"The whole thing's fallen through," said the spokeswoman late Monday evening. "The city basically realized that the agreement did not say the comptroller would not do his job; in fact the agreement said he could do his job, and that sort of surprised Randy Mastro, who had nonetheless sent us a letter saying he accepted the agreement," she said, referring to the New York City's deputy mayor for operations.

The Giuliani Administration, which has alleged some of McCall's audits were politically motivated because they focused on performance, had forced the state comptroller's staff to break them off, but on April 11, it announced that a pact had been reached.

A spokeswoman for New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said that McCall had agreed to withdraw audits that covered the police, the sanitation department, human resources, and on how the city is prepared to deal with computer problems that could arise at the beginning of the year 2000.
The state comptroller as soon as Tuesday was expected to seek legal remedies to force the city to allow it to continue with its audits.
